messages:
Maria (Finance): Heads up — saw an unexpected surcharge on the May APAC invoice. Line item called `accelerator-support-addon` applied twice for several GPU SKUs in ap-northeast1. Can ops confirm if we've enabled any marketplace support that might double-bill?
Aditya (CloudOps): Hmm, I can pull the billing export. Which invoice ID / sample lines?
Maria (Finance): Invoice 2024-05-23, sample lines below from export CSV: 
```
invoice_id,sku,region,description,amount
INV-20240523,accelerator-NVIDIA-A100,asia-northeast1,accelerator-support-addon,120.00
INV-20240523,accelerator-NVIDIA-A100,asia-northeast1,accelerator-support-addon,120.00
INV-20240523,accelerator-NVIDIA-A100,asia-northeast1,compute-accelerator-hour,240.00
```
Maria (Finance): Two identical support addon lines for the same SKU and period. Not showing as credits, just extra charge.
BillingBot: Automated alert: duplicate line heuristics matched for invoice INV-20240523 (confidence 0.87). Recommended: tag for manual review.
Kyle (Infra): We did enable a vendor-managed support package for a handful of clusters in ap-northeast1 last quarter. Also rolled out a private marketplace image that includes a support add-on. Could be both the provider and marketplace added the support charge.
Sophie (SRE): Stack-level note: GKE clusters using the marketplace image have nodepool labels that trigger a license/agent install. That agent is billed as "accelerator-support-addon" by the marketplace SKU. Meanwhile, provider-level addon is a separate support SKU. 
Aditya (CloudOps): Ok, immediate checks: 1) query BigQuery billing_export for duplicate SKU+resource_id for May 2024; 2) check marketplace subscription logs for any attached support add-ons; 3) confirm whether committed capacity credits applied separately. I'll run queries now.
Aditya (CloudOps): Query result snippet: found 78 distinct instances where marketplace_support and provider_support both billed against same instance_id for the week of May 18-24.
Maria (Finance): That explains the duplicate lines. Any idea why marketplace and provider both applied? Expected only marketplace or provider, not both.
Kyle (Infra): I think onboarding script accidentally left both flags enabled. Marketplace image auto-enrolls into vendor support; our provisioning policy also enabled provider-managed support on those nodepools. 
Sophie (SRE): Confirmed. When creating nodepool via terraform we set `enable_vendor_support = true` in the module and also applied `provider_support = true` via cluster policy for compliance. Two flags = two charges.
Maria (Finance): Rough estimate of impact?
Aditya (CloudOps): Preliminary tally: ~78 instances * $120 = $9,360 extra for May. Might be prorat-ed based on node uptime but ballpark.
Maria (Finance): Oof. Please add a column with resource_id in the export so we can map to customer/projects for chargeback.
Aditya (CloudOps): Will do. Also documenting remediation: 1) turn off provider_support flag for marketplace-enrolled nodepools; 2) add a provisioning guardrail to terraform module; 3) add validation in CI to prevent both flags.
Kyle (Infra): I'll open a small PR to the cluster module to refuse enabling both and set default to marketplace only for specific clusters.
Sophie (SRE): I'll patch the nodepool label script to set `provider_support=false` when `marketplace_image=true`.
Maria (Finance): For billing recourse: we should open a support case with provider asking for reversal/refund for duplicate lines and include the CSV evidence. Also check if any commitment/discounts were affected.
Aditya (CloudOps): Filing provider ticket now. Ticket #CLOUD-87219 created — included CSV export, BigQuery query, and sample invoice lines. Asking for review and refund.
BillingBot: Support ticket CLOUD-87219 status: created -> awaiting provider acknowledgement.
Maria (Finance): Thanks. Also tag accounting for potential credit processing. 
Kyle (Infra): PR #1183 created to enforce the single-support rule. Will merge after one LGTM.
Sophie (SRE): Deployed patch to label script; new nodepools will be safe. Running migration plan to update the 78 affected nodepools to prefer marketplace support and disable provider flag.
Aditya (CloudOps): Migration planned at 2am UTC to avoid disruption (maintenance window). Will monitor invoice export after run.
Maria (Finance): Once provider responds, let's confirm expected refund amount and expected timeline. If they decline, finance will request mediation.
Sophie (SRE): Quick note — do not disable both supports at once on a live nodepool. We'll do rolling updates and cordon drains.
Maria (Finance): Follow-up: Provider responded (support portal) requesting proof of duplicate charges and a mapping to instance IDs. I uploaded the export and BigQuery mapping. Awaiting final review.
Aditya (CloudOps): Provider acknowledged possible marketplace passthrough billing, escalated to billing team, ETA 5 business days.
Maria (Finance): Filing internal cost recovery note and tagging the affected product teams for chargebacks. Closing loop in 7 days or when provider completes refund.
Kyle (Infra): Action items: PR merged, migration scheduled, CI validation added.
Sophie (SRE): Migration completed (all 78 nodepools reconfigured), no downtime incidents reported.
Maria (Finance): Provider issued partial credit of $8,900 pending reversal — finance to reconcile. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
BillingBot: Ticket CLOUD-87219 status: resolved -> credit issued.
Maria (Finance): I'll mark this thread resolved once credits appear and accounting posts the reversal.
Aditya (CloudOps): Leaving a runbook entry under infra/runbooks/billing-dup-support-addons.md to prevent recurrence.
Maria (Finance): Great. Closing for now. If anyone sees similar patterns in other regions, please flag.
